titleText.es: Aparentemente, Google asume que viajarás durante las horas operativas del ferry. Perdimos dos horas rodeando ese maldito lago (por no hablar del Hombre de Paja).
titleText.en: Apparently Google assumes you're traveling during the ferry's normal operating hours. We lost two hours circling that damn lake (to say nothing of the Straw Man).
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive closely follows the official English title text and translates Straw Man literally as Hombre de Paja.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to cause; to give (in dar problemas)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dar usually means “to give.” In dar problemas, English naturally uses “cause” or “create” instead.
Before a place in a sequence, por can mark an approximate position rather than a route or cause.

example.es: La explicación aparece por la página diez.
example.en: The explanation appears around page ten.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Gira tells one familiar person to turn. It comes from girar, “to turn.”
Continúa tells one familiar person to continue. The written accent keeps the stress on ú.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: take (a form of transport; informal command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Toma tells one familiar person to use or board the named transport. It comes from tomar.
Ferry is a borrowed noun used in Spanish for a boat that carries passengers or vehicles across water.

example.es: El ferry sale a las nueve.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Atraviesa tells one familiar person to cross something from one side to the other.
With a vehicle or service, tomar means using it to travel.

example.en: We are going to take the train.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: past; later than (with a stated time)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Más normally means “more.” In a time expression such as es más de medianoche, it says the stated time has already passed.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links más to the time already passed
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish uses más de before the stated time; English can express the whole combination with “past.”
Da is a present form of dar. With a feeling such as miedo, English normally uses “causes,” “makes ... feel,” or a verb such as “scares.”
Guiaría combines guiar with the -ía ending to describe what someone or something would do.
Déjame joins the affirmative command deja, “let,” to me, which marks the person receiving permission. The accent keeps the original stress after the pronoun is attached.
Trepa tells one familiar person to climb. It comes from trepar.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: hanged man; person executed by hanging
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ahorcado comes from ahorcar, “to hang by the neck.” As a noun it can name a person who has been hanged.

example.es: La leyenda habla de un ahorcado.
example.en: The legend tells of a hanged man.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Evitando is evitar with the -ando ending, which presents the avoiding as accompanying another action.

example.es: Cruzó la plaza evitando la lluvia.
example.en: She crossed the square while avoiding the rain.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you arrive; you reach (special form for an event still ahead)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Llegues is a present subjunctive form of llegar. After cuando, it presents the arrival as a future event that has not happened yet.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: knock (on a door; informal singular command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Llamar usually means “to call.” In llamar a la puerta, it means knocking so that someone answers.

example.es: Llama a la puerta antes de entrar.
example.en: Knock on the door before entering.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pregunta tells one familiar person to ask. With por, it means asking to speak to or find someone.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: for; required after preguntar before the person sought
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Preguntar por alguien means asking to speak to, see, or locate that person.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: tell him/her; say to him/her (informal singular command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dile joins the command di, from decir, to le, which marks the person receiving the message.
Danzante can describe a person or thing that dances.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: they rest; they are at rest

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dará is the future form of dar used with one person or thing.

example.en: Ana will give you the key.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: As a warning by itself, cuidado means “careful” or “watch out.”

cardDefinitions.answerEn: go down; travel down (informal singular command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Baja tells one familiar person to move downward or along a descending route.
Here mina is the place where minerals are extracted, not the explosive device.
Espantapájaros combines a form related to espantar, “to scare away,” with pájaros, “birds.” The compound has the same form in singular and plural.

example.es: Hay un espantapájaros en el campo.
example.en: There is a scarecrow in the field.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you feel (special form for an event still ahead)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sientas is a present subjunctive form of sentir. After cuando, it presents the feeling as a future event that has not happened yet.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: your here; Spanish keeps “the” because te already marks the affected owner
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish often uses an article before a body part when me, te, le, nos, or les already identifies whose body is affected.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks helarse, “to freeze” or “go cold”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The small word se turns helar, “to freeze something,” into helarse, where the subject itself freezes or goes cold.
Hiela is a present form of helar. The e changes to ie in this form.

example.es: El lago se hiela en invierno.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: your here; Spanish uses “the” before body parts whose owner is already clear
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish commonly keeps the article before a body part and lets the surrounding pronoun or context identify the owner.
Detén is the command form of detener used with one familiar person. It takes a written accent.
Sal is the irregular command form of salir for one familiar person.
Quédate joins the command queda to te because the verb is quedarse, “to stay.” The accent preserves the original stress.
Without a following noun, este can name the cardinal direction east; this is different from este meaning “this.”

example.es: El sol sale por el este.
example.en: The sun rises in the east.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The -as ending matches a feminine plural noun.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks the person or thing feared with temerle
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In varieties that use temerle a, le appears with the verb and a introduces the feared target.

example.en: He is afraid of the dark.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Teme is a present form of temer used with one person or thing.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; combines a + el before what is feared after temerle
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In temerle a algo, the required a combines with el to form al before a masculine singular target.
Equipo can also mean equipment; here it names a group of people working together.

example.en: The team is looking for a solution.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ayudarte joins ayudar, “to help,” to te, “you.” Spanish writes the two pieces as one word.
Dominas is the ordinary present form of dominar for one familiar person.
Guiará combines the unchanged verb guiar with the -á future ending for one person or thing.
At the start of a stand-alone wish, que introduces the hoped-for event and is followed by a special subjunctive verb form.
Ayude is a present subjunctive form of ayudar. After wish-introducing que, it presents the helping as something hoped for.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something causes trouble or creates problems?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of dar followed by problema or problemas.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dar literally means “to give,” but dar problemas is the conventional way to say that something causes trouble. Dar changes for the person, thing, and time; problemas stays a noun.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: girar a la izquierda / a la derecha
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you tell someone to turn left or right?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of girar, then a la izquierda for left or a la derecha for right.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Only girar changes for the person and time. The directional part stays a la izquierda or a la derecha; the a is part of this standard navigation expression.

example.es: Gira a la derecha en la esquina.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is scary or frightens someone?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Name the scary thing, use the matching form of dar, and add miedo. Use me, te, le, nos, os, or les when you need to name who feels afraid.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish presents the source of fear as “giving fear.” Dar changes for that source; miedo stays unchanged. The small person marker identifies who feels the fear and can be omitted for a general statement.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone lets another person do something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of dejar, mark the person receiving permission with me, te, le, nos, os, or les, and put the allowed action in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The unchanged dictionary form is the verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. The person marker can stand before a changed form of dejar, join an affirmative command such as déjame, or in some structures join the following dictionary-form verb. Dejar changes for the person and time; the allowed action does not.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you ask to speak to, see, or find a particular person?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of preguntar, then por, then the person.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Preguntar alone means “to ask.” Preguntar por alguien conventionally means asking for that person or asking where that person is. Preguntar changes for the person and time; por stays unchanged.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone's blood runs cold from fear?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of helarse with la sangre, and use me, te, le, nos, os, or les to mark the person who feels the fear.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Helar literally means “to freeze.” Se makes it helarse, where the blood itself goes cold, and the person marker identifies whose reaction it is. The form of helar changes for the time; sangre is singular, so the verb is singular.

example.es: Al oír el grito, se me heló la sangre.
example.en: When I heard the scream, my blood ran cold.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone is afraid of a particular person or thing using temerle?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of temer with le or les, then a before the person or thing that is feared.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In varieties that use this pattern, le or les appears with temer and a introduces the feared target. Temer changes for who feels the fear; le or les matches the target as singular or plural. Other varieties also use temer directly without le and a.

example.en: Marta is afraid of the dog.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say what will happen if a real possibility occurs?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use si with an ordinary present-time verb form for the condition, then state the result with a future form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Si introduces a condition treated as genuinely possible. Spanish normally keeps the verb immediately after si in the present form, not the future. The result can use the future, built here by keeping the action verb and adding an ending such as -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, or -án.

example.en: If you finish early, we will have dinner together.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you express a stand-alone hope or wish for someone?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Begin with que, name who or what the wish concerns, and use a special subjunctive form for the hoped-for action.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The subjunctive is a special verb form used here because the event is wished for rather than stated as fact. For example, tener changes to tengas and ayudar changes to ayude. This stand-alone que does not need a preceding verb meaning “I hope.”

example.en: May you have a good trip.
